When you use `malloc` (which stands for "memory allocation"), you are asking the computer to set aside a specific "room" in its memory for your program to store data. We use `malloc` when we don't know exactly how much memory we need until the program is actually running. For example, if you are writing a program to process a list of names, you might not know if the user will enter 10 names or 10,000 names. `malloc` allows you to request exactly the right amount of space on the fly, rather than guessing a fixed size ahead of time.
